references.text: Elijah then saw a small cloud rise from the sea, and soon the sky was black with clouds and it rained. Jesus refers to the common experience that clouds from the west (from the Mediterranean) bring rain, which is well illustrated in this story ([ref:1 Kings 18:44-45|1 Kings 18:44-45]).

Parallel text where Jesus says something similar to the Pharisees and Sadducees: they can interpret the appearance of the sky and predict the weather, but cannot interpret the signs of the times ([ref:Matt 16:2-3|Matthew 16:2-3]).

Jesus calls his listeners hypocrites because they can interpret the appearance of the earth and sky, but cannot interpret the present time ([ref:Luke 12:56|Luke 12:56]). This is the conclusion of the illustration that begins in verse 54.
Job describes the south wind as making clothes warm, a reference to natural observation of weather – related to Jesus' point that people know how to read natural signs ([ref:Job 37:17|Job 37:17]).
Continuation of Jesus' speech, where he mentions the south wind bringing heat – yet another example that people can interpret weather conditions ([ref:Luke 12:55|Luke 12:55]).
